title: Wasp Is Now Friendlier To AI Agents
summary: Wasp 0.26 makes it easy for agents to work on different tasks in your Wasp project at the same time using Git worktrees. You can now have your orchestrator run multiple worktrees and agents, each using wasp start and wasp start db without stepping on each other's toes.
body_markdown:
Wasp 0.26 improves support for agent orchestrators and running multiple instances of a Wasp project in Git worktrees:


- Incompatible Wasp commands no longer interfere with each other. For example, executing` wasp build` when` wasp start` is already running won't corrupt the generated code.
- Wasp no longer runs into *"Port is already taken"* errors when agents spin up multiple dev servers across worktrees. Both` wasp start` and` wasp start db` now dynamically look for free ports.


## What are Git worktrees and why do agent orchestrators need them?​


Before we dig into the new features, let's quickly discuss agent orchestrators and Git worktrees.


If you know all about this, feel free to skip right to thenext section . If not, here's a refresher:


- An **agent orchestrator** is a tool for coordinating agents. It helps you assign tasks to agents and keep track of their work, without juggling thirteen terminal windows and losing your mind. Examples of popular agent orchestrators are[Herdr](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr) ,[Workmux](https://github.com/raine/workmux) , and[Conductor](https://www.conductor.build/) .
- **[Git worktrees](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree)** are a Git feature that lets you check out multiple branches of a Git project at the same time, each branch in its own directory.


Developers use agent orchestrators to simultaneously work on multiple features. The usual workflow looks like this:


1. The orchestrator gives each agent an isolated Git worktree.
2. Each agent works on a feature inside its worktree.
3. The orchestrator lets you know whenever an agent needs your input.
4. When a feature is done, you review the diff and use the orchestrator to merge it into` main` , deleting the agent's worktree.


## What's new in Wasp?​


Previous versions of Wasp didn't have great out-of-the-box support for orchestrator workflows. You *could* set them up, but the process was more involved than we would have liked.


With Wasp 0.26, you can let your agents loose in as many Git worktrees as you want. They'll stay out of each other's way.


## How to use this?​


There's nothing special you need to do. Just keep running Wasp commands as you've always done and leave the rest to Wasp.


Read on to understand what makes this experience possible.


### Wasp commands no longer fight over the file system​


Before Wasp 0.26, running multiple Wasp commands in the same project could cause them to write over each other's outputs. For example, executing` wasp build` would break an already running instance of` wasp start` .


Wasp 0.26 prevents such conflicts:


Conflicting commands in the same project: Wasp now blocks the second one instead of letting it corrupt the output.


If someone runs two different commands that write to the same files, Wasp catches it and prints a clear error message. Both you and your agents can then decide what to do about it:


Terminal 1


```text
$   wasp start


🐝 --- Starting compilation and setup phase. Hold tight... ------------------------


🐝 --- Compiling wasp project... --------------------------------------------------


[      Wasp      ]   Starting npm install


```


Terminal 2


```text
$   wasp build


❌ --- [Error] Wasp project is already in use: ------------------------------------


Another Wasp command (PID 12345) is already running for this project. Stop it before running this command.


```


### Wasp projects no longer fight over ports​


Before Wasp 0.26, running` wasp start` and` wasp start db` in multiple worktrees was... problematic. All clients would fight over port 3000, all servers over 3001, and all databases over 5432. This led to many *"Port is already taken"* errors.


Wasp 0.26 solves this problem with dynamic port allocation.


If you've built a bespoke system for handling port conflicts, it's finally time to retire it. Just run the commands you want to run, and Wasp takes care of the rest:


```text
# Starts the client and the server on the first two free ports it finds.      # It starts looking at 3000 and goes up.     wasp start        # Starts the dev database on the first free port it finds.      # It starts looking at 5432 and goes up.     wasp start db
```


Two worktrees running at the same time: each process now takes the next free port.


That said, there are three things to keep in mind.


- First, your Wasp processes will no longer always run on the same ports (i.e.,` 3000` for the client,` 3001` for the server, and` 5432` for the dev database). They'll run on the first available ports starting from those, so pay attention to where Wasp tells you they're listening.
- Second, since each worktree gets its own database, working in many worktrees means having many databases. Databases are not terribly useful without data, so we recommend you[seed them](https://wasp.sh/docs/features/data/databases#seeding-the-database) .
- Third, because Wasp now manages the ports and URLs in development, setting them yourself (e.g.,` server.port` in` vite.config.ts` or` PORT` in` .env.server` ) is an error. This is a **breaking change.** Check the[migration guide](https://wasp.sh/docs/migration-guide) for the full list of changes and how to update your project. If your app needs to be reachable at a different address (e.g., a LAN hostname or an HTTPS tunnel), use the new` --client-url` and` --server-url` flags instead.


### Bonus feature​


Wasp 0.26 allows you to specify the exact development ports you want Wasp to use for your client, server, and database. The client and server flags work for both` wasp start` and` wasp build start` :


```text
wasp start --client-port   4000   --server-port   5000     wasp build start --client-port   4000   --server-port   5000     wasp start db --db-port   6000
```


If any of those ports is taken, Wasp will fail instead of looking for alternatives. The reasoning is that you care about your process running on those specific ports, so it's better to explicitly fail than silently start listening elsewhere. It's therefore up to you to either free those ports up, specify different ports, or remove the port arguments.


The` --db-port` flag was contributed by[Nihal Ahamed](https://github.com/Nihal-Ahamed-MS) . Thanks for all the patience during the design changes and reviews, Nihal!


## Try it out​


Parallel worktree support is live in Wasp 0.26. If you're not on it yet, update your Wasp CLI:


```text
npm   i   -g   @wasp.sh/wasp-cli
```


If you haven't set up worktrees for your Wasp project yet, the[Git worktree setup](https://wasp.sh/docs/advanced/git-worktrees) guide walks you through it.


Wasp 0.26 also brings` wasp show` , safer auth defaults, and a new docs structure. Check out the[Wasp 0.26 changelog](https://wasp.sh/blog/2026/10/23/wasp-0-26-changelog) for the full list.


We'd love to hear how it works for you - come chat with us on[Discord](https://discord.gg/rzdnErX) !
